facts.text: Christchurch, Virginia, takes its name from Christ Church Parish, founded on January 29, 1666, during a General Vestry meeting at Rosegill.
The current Christ Church building, completed in the 1720s, showcases Flemish‑bond brickwork and was overseen by mason Alexander Graves and carpenter John Hipkins, Sr.
Christchurch School, established in 1921 by Bishop William Cabell Brown, occupies 125 acres of waterfront and uses the Rappahannock River for sailing and environmental science lessons.
The churchyard contains an exceptional collection of 18th‑century tombstones, especially those of the Wormeley family, highlighting the area’s colonial heritage.
Christchurch lies on Virginia State Route 33, just 3.1 miles southeast of Urbanna, and sits on the south bank of the Rappahannock River in the Middle Peninsula.
After the American Revolution, the original church fell into disuse but was restored in 1843 following the parish’s revival in 1840.
